newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian banks ready for euro launch - CBF.
newsitem.headline: Belgian banks ready for euro launch - CBF.

text.p: Belgian banks say they are ready for payments, savings and lending in Europe's new single currency, the euro, from January 1, 1999, the sector's supervisor said, quoting the results of a recent poll.
"We are very satisfied and confident," chairman Jean-Louis Duplat of the the Banking and Finance Commission (CBF) told a news conference on 1996 and early 1997 trends on Monday.

He said the CBF poll, conducted in recent weeks, showed the sector expected overall costs to be 21 billion Belgian francs ($572 million) for the period until 2002. Duplat noted this included costs for adapting computer equipment to the change of millennium.

As a result of the launch of the euro and having to deal with the so-called millennium bug, banks said they would have to revise their planning for information technology development and postpone a number of projects in the years ahead.

Banks said they were counting on "certain revenue losses", mainly in the area of foreign exchange, Duplat said. They expected to compensate for these losses by curbing their trading rooms and back offices and streamlining information technology.
"Banks will further improve cost control," he said. In addition, they would seek to develop business outside the euro zone.
Full details of the poll are due to be published this autumn.
